label: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
claim: In the BETSE model of the Xenopus neurula, HCN2 channels open at hyperpolarized membrane voltage and hyperpolarize further when open, so they act as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small existing Vmem gradients: sufficiently negative neural tube cells go very hyperpolarized while depolarized lateral regions are left unchanged.
quote: HCN2 channels are predicted to open at hyperpolarized Vmem, generating more hyperpolarization with opening, thereby serving as a Vmem-controlled switch of Vmem state, capable of amplifying small Vmem gradients, similar to IT effect (Fig. 3c, e, f).
scope: BETSE bioelectric model of an anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula
measurable_quantities: simulated Vmem by region with and without HCN2
candidate_data: BETSE (open-source simulator) to re-run the model with the published parameters (Table 1, Supplementary Note).

label: Measured HCN2 hyperpolarization in vivo was about half the model's prediction
claim: Hcn2 mRNA injection hyperpolarized the neural Vmem signal of Xenopus embryos by about 15 mV relative to controls, whereas the BETSE model predicted about 30 mV.
quote: However, the extent of enhanced hyperpolarization predicted by BETSE model for IT and HCN2 was higher (~30 mV) than actually observed (~15 mV) (Figs. 3e and 4).
scope: Xenopus laevis neurula-stage embryos injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA
measurable_quantities: neural plate Vmem (voltage dye calibrated by whole-cell recording)
candidate_data: New voltage-dye imaging of Hcn2-injected Xenopus embryos; BETSE re-runs for the predicted value.

label: HCN2 expression restores the neural Vmem prepattern despite nicotine
claim: In nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos, expression of HCN2 channels enhances the neural-tube-specific hyperpolarization and restores the endogenous Vmem prepattern that nicotine otherwise suppresses, as the BETSE model predicted.
quote: As predicted, nicotine exposure suppresses the neural brain-specific Vmem pattern, while HCN2 channel expression enhances the neural Vmem pattern and restores it even in presence of the otherwise teratogenic nicotine.
scope: Xenopus laevis neurula-stage embryos exposed to nicotine, with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA
measurable_quantities: neural plate and ectoderm Vmem by voltage dye and whole-cell recording
candidate_data: New voltage imaging in Xenopus embryos; no public Vmem map dataset for this condition is known.

label: HCN2 reduces even minor background brain defects in untreated embryos
claim: In untreated Xenopus embryos, Hcn2 mRNA injection reduced the incidence of minor deviations from ideal brain morphology from about 9% to about 1.5%, so HCN2 improved patterning beyond that of unperturbed controls.
quote: Thus, misexpression of HCN2 channels resulted in an improvement of developmental patterning even beyond that observed in control populations of unperturbed embryos raised under optimal conditions.
scope: Wild-type Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA, scored at stage 45
measurable_quantities: incidence of minor brain morphology deviations
candidate_data: New Xenopus injection experiments scored for brain morphology; Xenbase for staging references.

label: HCN2 fully rescues nicotine-induced brain malformations to control levels
claim: Injection of Hcn2-WT mRNA into nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos reduced the incidence of major brain morphology defects from about 60% to about 6%, indistinguishable from untreated controls (about 7%).
quote: Remarkably, Hcn2-WT mRNA-injected embryos showed a complete rescue of brain morphology defects from nicotine exposure, to levels (~6%) indistinguishable from that of untreated control embryos (~7%) (Fig. 5f).
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA
measurable_quantities: incidence of major brain morphology defects at stage 45
candidate_data: Independent replication in Xenopus; no deposited per-embryo scoring data are named in the text.

label: Dominant-negative HCN2 does not rescue nicotine brain defects
claim: Nicotine-exposed Xenopus embryos injected with a dominant-negative, non-conducting HCN2 mutant showed no rescue of brain morphology defects (about 70% defective), so the rescue depends on HCN2 channel conductance.
quote: In contrast, nicotine-exposed embryos injected with a mutant, dominant-negative form of HCN2 failed to show rescue of brain morphology defects (~70%) (Fig. 5f).
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), injected with Hcn2-DN (GYG→AAA pore mutant) mRNA
measurable_quantities: incidence of major brain morphology defects

label: HCN2 restores wild-type brain shape in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claim: Geometric morphometrics of stage-45 tadpoles show that nicotine significantly changes brain shape relative to the head, while nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA do not differ in shape from controls.
quote: Thus, nicotine significantly changes brain shape, but Hcn2-WT mRNA microinjections restore brain morphology to the wild-type state.
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to nicotine (0.1 mg/mL, stages 10–35), with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA
candidate_data: Landmark images of tadpoles would be needed; MorphoJ for reanalysis; no public landmark dataset named.

label: HCN2 restores learning in nicotine-exposed tadpoles
claim: In an automated red-light avoidance assay, only about 12% of nicotine-exposed Xenopus tadpoles learned, versus 100% of controls, and about 85% of nicotine-exposed tadpoles injected with Hcn2-WT mRNA learned.
quote: However, nicotine-exposed embryos receiving Hcn2-WT mRNA showed significant improvement in learning ability (85%, n = 20) in comparison to nicotine-exposed tadpoles (Fig. 7b, c, ANOVA, p < 0.001).
scope: Morphologically normal Xenopus laevis tadpoles exposed to nicotine as embryos, with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA
measurable_quantities: fraction of tadpoles reaching the red-avoidance learning criterion
candidate_data: New behavioural trials with an automated training apparatus.

label: HCN2 rescue corrects otx2 and xbf1 expression after nicotine
claim: Nicotine reduces or mispatterns expression of the forebrain/midbrain transcription factors otx2 and xbf1 in Xenopus embryos, and Hcn2-WT mRNA injection restores their normal expression, linking HCN2-mediated repair to the known genetic cascade of brain patterning.
quote: Thus, HCN2 channel rescue of nicotine-induced defects includes correction of otx2 and xbf1, connecting HCN2-mediated repair of brain to the known molecular-genetic cascade of brain patterning factors.
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos at stage 25, nicotine-exposed from stage 10, with or without Hcn2-WT mRNA
measurable_quantities: fraction of embryos with reduced or mispatterned otx2, xbf1, emx and pax6 in situ signal
candidate_data: Xenbase gene expression and in situ resources for otx2 and xbf1 (foxg1) as references; new in situ experiments.

label: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
claim: Because a dominant-negative HCN2 construct does not disrupt brain patterning, native HCN2 channel activity is not required for normal Xenopus brain patterning, ruling out the possibility that nicotine causes defects by directly blocking endogenous HCN2.
quote: However, our experiments with dominant-negative HCN2 channel shows that native HCN2 channel activity is not required for proper brain patterning (Supplementary Figure 4), thus negating this possibility.
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with Hcn2-DN mRNA
measurable_quantities: incidence of brain morphology defects with Hcn2-DN alone
candidate_data: Xenbase expression data for hcn2 in early embryos; new dominant-negative or knockdown experiments.

label: HCN2's restorative action may extend to many teratogens and lesions
claim: The authors suggest that HCN2's ability to improve brain morphology even in control embryos points to a general mechanism, reinforcing endogenous bioelectric signals needed for correct brain morphology, that could repair defects caused by a wide range of teratogens or physiological and genetic lesions, not only nicotine.
quote: These observations suggest that the restorative action of HCN2 is not limited to nicotine-induced brain morphology defects, but could reveal a more general mechanism of action, reinforcing the endogenous bioelectrical signals required for correct developmental brain morphology that might be partially destabilized by a wide range of exogenous teratogens or endogenous physiological/genetic lesions.
scope: Developing vertebrate brain (shown in Xenopus) exposed to teratogens or carrying physiological or genetic lesions
measurable_quantities: brain defect incidence after various teratogens with and without HCN2 expression
candidate_data: Published follow-up studies of HCN2 rescue with other teratogens; new Xenopus experiments.

label: Reagents that sharpen bioelectric compartment borders reinforce normal patterning
claim: The BETSE model predicts that reagents that sharpen the borders between bioelectric compartments, such as the context-sensitive HCN2 channel, will reinforce normal developmental patterning, a prediction confirmed for HCN2 in vivo.
quote: Most importantly, it predicts that reagents that sharpen borders between bioelectric compartments will reinforce normal patterning, thus identifying a context-sensitive HCN2 ion channel as an intervention tool.
scope: Embryonic brain patterning in Xenopus; proposed more generally for bioelectrically patterned tissues
measurable_quantities: patterning defect incidence after interventions that change that contrast
candidate_data: BETSE simulations; new perturbation experiments with other context-sensitive channels.
